sections.title: From font bytes to a glyph request
sections.prose: Font bytes enter through `new_memory_face`: it passes `data`, `face_index`, and `size_pt` to `Font::memory_face`, then wraps the parsed font in a `Face` with a fresh render-font cache. Opening therefore selects and initializes a face; it does not itself produce glyph pixels. Inside `memory_face`, format probes send recognized PCF, PFR, WinFNT, BDF, CID Type 1, Type 42 (`type42_face`), and Type 1 data to their respective constructors; other inputs reach `truetype_face`. If that parse fails and the bytes are at least 118 long, `winfnt_face` gets a fallback attempt, but the original error normally wins unless the fallback reports an unknown format for a WinFNT-shaped header. A glyph index and `LoadFlags` enter through `load_glyph`, which forwards to `load_glyph_with_transform` and then `load_glyph_from_font`; an unmatched `sbix` strike can fail early, and `NO_RECURSE` suppresses the transform. When `render_requested` is true and an outline is available, the code applies any transform and sends that outline to `render_loaded_outline`, then stores the resulting bitmap in the glyph slot.
